string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is China\'s capital and one of its four centrally administered municipalities. It is in northern China and serves as the country\'s political center. The municipal government also describes Beijing as a center for culture, international exchange, science and technology. The city has 16 districts, from busy central neighborhoods to mountain areas on its edge. Its long history can be seen at places such as the Forbidden City, the Temple of Heaven and sections of the Great Wall. Today, historic sites, universities, research centers and modern business areas are all part of city life.

Shanghai sits at the mouth of the Yangtze River in eastern China and is part of the Yangtze River Delta. It is one of China\'s centrally administered municipalities and has 16 districts. The city grew as a port and remains an important place for shipping, trade and finance. Pudong\'s newer buildings stand across the river from older streets and the Bund waterfront. Shanghai also has universities, museums, theaters, parks and many local neighborhoods. Its location, transport links and mix of old and new areas make it an important business and cultural center in China.

Chongqing is a municipality in southwest China, in the upper Yangtze River region. The Yangtze and Jialing rivers meet in the city, and the surrounding hills give many streets steep slopes and views over the water. The municipality covers a wide area that includes urban districts, towns and countryside. Chongqing is an important transport and manufacturing center in western China, with rail, road and river connections. The city\'s history, food and river setting are part of its local character. Visitors often notice the bridges, hillside neighborhoods and busy evening streets, as well as its well-known hot-pot dishes.

Tianjin is a municipality in northern China, close to Beijing and the Bohai Sea. The city developed on a broad plain crossed by rivers, including the Haihe, and its position helped connect inland routes with coastal trade. Tianjin is now an important port and industrial center. Its recorded history as a garrison began in 1404 during the Ming dynasty, and the city\'s name is commonly linked to the emperor\'s river crossing. Historic streets and buildings sit alongside newer districts. The waterfront, museums and local food show different parts of Tianjin\'s past and present.
